title: Dense quality overhaul step 3: GPU TSDF fusion with voxel hashing
abstract:
Implements step 3 of the dense quality overhaul (`docs/dense-mvs.md` 10.4, accepted 2026-10-21): a TSDF fusion with voxel hashing, free-space carving and voxel levels by distance. It is the option `fusion: 'tsdf'` of `reconstructDenseGpu`, and the lab's default fusion from now on. The step record is in 10.8 ("Step 3 record").

## What was built
- Kernels: `src/gpu/tsdf.shade.ts` (`tsdfAllocate`, `tsdfAssign`, `tsdfIntegrate`, `tsdfCarve`, `tsdfExtract`). Blocks of 8×8×8 voxels sit in an open-addressing table, at 4 levels (v_L = v_0·2^L). The sums are integer `atomicAdd`s, so their result does not depend on the order of the invocations. The layout is in 4.1.
- Host: `src/gpu/tsdf.ts` (`fuseTsdfGpu`). It counts the blocks with a dry run and cuts the volume into boxes that fit the budget (#160). Each box has a margin of one block. The budget changes the speed and never the points.
- CPU reference and planner: `src/reconstruction/tsdf.ts` (`fuseTsdf`, `planTsdfVolume`, `planTsdfBoxes`).
- The confidence of 10.3 is the integration weight. The filter writes it to `mvsCost` when the run asks for it, in window mode and in streamed mode.
- `scripts/eth3d-dense.mjs`: `--save-maps` writes the filtered maps after a run. `--maps` fuses saved maps without the depth stage.
- Lab: TSDF is the default fusion. `?denseFusion=pixel` selects 3.10. The 3.12 cleanup runs by default after the pixel fusion only. `?denseClean=1|0` overrides that. The run record has a new field, `dense.options.fusion`.
- The library default stays `'pixel'`.

## ETH3D `pipes` (SwiftShader, 14 views, scale 8, the same saved depth maps)
| Cloud | Points | F 1/2/5/10 cm | Acc 2 cm | Compl 2 cm | Landmarks uncovered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pixel fusion, raw (baseline) | 156,751 | 33.7 / 45.9 / 59.6 / 67.4 | 83.3 | 31.7 | 42.1 % |
| Pixel + lab cleanup | 70,302 | 27.2 / 34.5 / 41.7 / 47.7 | 87.6 | 21.5 | 61.3 % |
| **TSDF, raw** | 99,674 | 40.6 / 54.0 / 67.3 / 74.6 | 69.0 | 44.4 | 27.0 % |
| TSDF + lab cleanup | 60,140 | 39.2 / 51.8 / 62.7 / 67.8 | 72.7 | 40.2 | 36.2 % |

Fusion stage time and dispatches:
- Pixel fusion: 97 to 118 s with about 16,000 dispatches (the baseline record had 173 s).
- TSDF: 20.5 s with 343 dispatches, in 2 passes.

The container is shared with other agents, so these times are noisy (±30 % or more). The TSDF fusion's peak device bytes are 136.8 MB at a 256 MiB budget, and 59.4 MB at a quarter of the blocks per pass. Both give the same cloud.

Proof criterion of 10.4: met. The accuracy is lower than the pixel fusion's (69.0 against 83.3 at 2 cm), and this is recorded as open.

## Checks run (2026-10-21, at `05a9adf` or an earlier commit with the same source)
- `npm run format:check`: pass.
- `npm run typecheck`: pass.
- `cd website && npx tsc --noEmit`: pass.
- `npm test`: 224/224.
- `npm run build`: pass.
- `npm run build:website`: pass.
- `npm run test:shade`: 193/193, including `tests/typeshade/tsdf.test.mjs`.
- `npm run test:webgpu`: 46/46, including `tests/typeshade/tsdf-webgpu.test.mjs`.
- `npm run test:website`:
  - 159/161 in the full run, under load.
  - The two failures passed when run alone: the 3D card layout test (6 px, which depends on the load) and the public UI test, after its expected options were updated for the new lab default in `05a9adf`.

## Open
- The TSDF accuracy gap. Candidates: a `minWeight` that counts views, and step 4 (10.5).
- Carving takes 62 % of the kernel time.
- The pixel fusion's dispatch count comes from the same chunk-sizing effect. It is not changed here.
- Not run: a physical GPU, and the lab on a device.
